discussions.title: Welcome! Start here

posts.text:
Welcome to the community! This is a friendly place for people who like making things: photos, food, gardens, bike rides, and the occasional fight with a router.

**A few things to know:**

- Pick a tag when you start a discussion, so the right people see it.
- In **Tech Help**, mark the reply that solved your problem as the best answer. It helps the next person.
- Be kind. Everyone here was a beginner at something.

Say hello in the introductions, and enjoy.
Thanks for setting this up! Already found three discussions I want to read.
Glad to be here. Is there a way to follow a single tag? I mostly care about Photography and Books.
{{p:3}} Yes: open the tag and use the bell next to its name. You can follow new discussions, or every reply if you like to keep up with everything.

discussions.title: Golden hour in the city: share your shots

posts.text:
I love the twenty minutes before sunset, when the whole skyline turns warm. Post your golden hour city pictures here! Not mine, but this one is my benchmark:

{{img:city}}
That light on the glass is unreal. What do you all use for exposure in that situation? My phone always blows out the sky.
{{p:2}} Expose for the brightest part of the sky and lift the shadows later. On a phone, tap the sky and drag the exposure slider down a little before you shoot.
And shoot a few minutes *after* you think it's over. The blue hour that follows is often better.
{{p:4}} Agreed, the blue hour is underrated. Going out on Friday to try it at the harbour.

discussions.title: First mirrorless camera under $800?

posts.text: I've outgrown my phone and want a first proper camera. Budget is about $800, used is fine. Mostly travel and my kids running around. Where would you start?
For kids running around, autofocus matters more than anything else. Look at the last generation of any big brand's entry model, used. You'll get a better body for the money.
Spend less on the body and more on one good lens. A fast 35 mm (or the equivalent for your sensor) will change your pictures more than any body upgrade.
Also check how the camera feels in your hand before you buy. The best camera is the one you actually take with you.
Thank you all! Found a used body with a 35 mm lens for $720. {{p:3}} you were right, the lens makes all the difference.

discussions.title: How do you back up your photo library?

posts.text: My library is about 900 GB and lives on one external drive. I know, I know. What's a sensible setup that doesn't cost a fortune every month?

The usual rule is 3-2-1: three copies, on two kinds of storage, one of them somewhere else. For you that could be the drive, a second drive at a friend's place, and a cloud copy of just your favourites.
Whatever you do, test a restore once. A backup you've never restored from is a hope, not a backup.
Bought a second drive and set up a weekly sync. Restoring a test folder worked. Marking {{p:2}} as the answer, thanks both!

discussions.title: What's your go-to weeknight dinner?

posts.text: Thirty minutes, one pan, five hungry people. Mine is chickpeas with spinach, smoked paprika and a lot of garlic, with bread to mop it up. What's yours?
Fried rice with whatever's in the fridge. Day-old rice is the secret, fresh rice goes mushy.
Peanut stew. Onion, tomato, peanut butter, stock, sweet potato, whatever greens I have. Fifteen minutes of work.
Kimchi fried rice with a fried egg on top. {{p:2}} same rule about the rice!
Pasta with butter, black pepper and too much cheese. I'm not proud.
Dal. It's cheap, it freezes well, and you can make it as simple or fancy as you want.
{{p:3}} I made the peanut stew last night. The kids asked for it again tomorrow, which never happens. Thank you!

discussions.title: Cast iron care: did I ruin my pan?

posts.text: I left my new cast iron pan soaking overnight and now it has orange rust spots all over. Is it ruined?
Not at all, it's just surface rust. Scrub it off with steel wool, dry the pan on the hob, rub in a very thin layer of oil and heat it until it smokes. Repeat two or three times.
And don't soak it again. Wash it quickly while it's warm, dry it on the heat, tiny bit of oil. That's the whole routine.
The more you cook in it, the better it gets. Fry some potatoes in it this week and it'll be fine.

It worked! Re-seasoned it and made cornbread to celebrate.

{{img:cornbread}}

discussions.title: Fermentation corner: kimchi, sauerkraut and friends

posts.text: Sauerkraut person here. Two percent salt by weight and patience, that's all.
How do you stop the top from going mouldy? Mine always gets a white film after a week.
{{p:3}} Keep everything under the brine with a weight. A white film is usually harmless yeast you can skim off, but anything fuzzy or coloured means start again.
A small zip bag filled with brine makes a perfect weight, by the way.

discussions.title: Sourdough starter not rising after a week

posts.text: Day seven. My starter bubbled a lot on days two and three, then went completely flat. I feed it 50 g flour and 50 g water every day. What am I doing wrong?
Nothing, probably! That early burst is often bacteria, not yeast. The quiet phase is normal. Keep feeding and it should come back in a few days.
Two things that helped me: some wholemeal or rye flour in the feed, and a warmer spot. Mine woke up when I moved it on top of the fridge.
Also discard most of it before each feed, otherwise the new flour gets diluted.
Day eleven: it doubled in six hours! {{p:3}} the top of the fridge did it. First loaf this weekend.

discussions.title: Tomatoes splitting after the heat wave

posts.text: Yes, eat them soon. Splitting happens when the plant suddenly gets lots of water after a dry spell: the inside grows faster than the skin.
Water deeply and regularly, and mulch the soil so it doesn't swing from bone dry to soaked. Pick fruit when it's just turning if heavy rain is forecast.
Mulched with straw and set a watering schedule. No new splits this week!

discussions.title: Balcony herb garden: what actually survives?

posts.text: South-facing balcony, very windy, I'm away a lot in summer. Which herbs survive me?
Rosemary, thyme and sage love sun and forgive you for forgetting them. Basil and coriander will not.
Chives come back every year and handle wind fine. Mint too, but give it its own pot or it takes over.
Self-watering pots changed everything for me. Two weeks away and the oregano didn't even notice.
Rosemary, thyme and chives in self-watering pots it is. {{p:4}} thanks for the tip!

discussions.title: Saving seeds from this year's harvest

posts.text: I'd like to save seeds from my best beans and tomatoes for next year. Anything I should know before I start?
Only save from open-pollinated varieties. Seeds from F1 hybrids won't grow true to the parent.
For tomatoes, ferment the seeds in a little water for a few days, rinse, and dry them on a plate. It gets rid of the gel that stops them sprouting.
Beans are drying in paper bags and the tomato seeds are fermenting. The kitchen smells interesting.

discussions.title: Commuting by bike through winter: tips?

posts.text: Last winter I gave up in December. This year I want to make it through. What made the difference for you?
Lights, mudguards and good gloves, in that order. Bright rear light that also blinks in daylight.
Studded tyres if you get ice. They feel slow, but nothing beats staying upright.
Also: keep a spare set of dry clothes at work. Arriving wet is what really kills motivation.
Ordered studded tyres and proper mudguards. {{u:theo}} I'll report back in January!

discussions.title: Tubeless tyres: worth switching?

posts.text: Three punctures this month on my commute. Everyone tells me to go tubeless. Is it really worth the hassle?
For commuting, yes. Small holes seal themselves and you often don't even notice. Setting it up the first time is messy, though.
Top up the sealant every few months, it dries out. And carry a plug kit for bigger holes.
Convinced. Doing it this weekend, wish me luck.

discussions.title: Recommend a sci-fi novel for someone new to the genre

posts.text: My partner has never read science fiction and asked me for a first book. She loves character-driven literary fiction. Where would you start her?
Something where the science stays in the background and the people come first. A quiet novel about a generation ship or a first-contact story told by a linguist would be perfect.
Short stories are a great way in, too. She can try several flavours and see what she likes.
Great ideas. She started with a short story collection and is already asking for more. {{p:3}} spot on.

discussions.title: Laptop fan constantly running after update

posts.text: Since the last system update my laptop fan runs at full speed all the time, even when I'm only reading email. Any ideas?
Right after a big update, the system often reindexes your files in the background for a day or two. Leave it plugged in overnight and see if it calms down.
If it doesn't, open the activity monitor or task manager and sort by CPU. Something stuck at 100% is usually the culprit.
It was the indexing! Quiet since this morning. Thanks {{u:dmitri}}.

discussions.title: Best way to share large video files with family?

posts.text: I've got 40 GB of videos from my sister's wedding and family in three countries who want them. Email obviously won't work. What's the easiest way for non-technical people?
A shared folder on any cloud storage service, with a link they can open in the browser. Nobody needs an account or an app.
If storage is a problem, compress them first. Wedding videos straight off a camera are huge, and a modern format halves them with no visible difference.
And put a short note in the folder explaining which file is which. Grandparents will thank you.
Shared folder sent, with a note. Even my uncle managed to download them. Thank you!

discussions.title: Router keeps dropping Wi-Fi every evening

posts.text: Every evening around 8 pm our Wi-Fi drops for a minute or two, several times. Daytime is fine. The provider says the line is OK.
Sounds like interference: everyone in your building is home and on Wi-Fi at the same time. Try changing the channel in the router settings, or use 5 GHz if your devices support it.
Also check for a firmware update for the router. Mine had a bug that caused exactly this.
Switched to a quieter 5 GHz channel. Three evenings without a drop! Marking this solved and locking it.

discussions.title: Password manager recommendations

posts.text: I finally want to stop reusing passwords. What should I look for in a password manager?
That it works on all your devices, has a good track record, and supports passkeys. Then turn on two-factor authentication for the manager itself.
And don't try to change every password on day one. Update each one the next time you log in to that site. It gets done without the pain.
